sutta: 4.20. On one occasion, the Blessed One was dwelling among the Kosalans in a small forest hut in the Himalayan region. Then when the Blessed One was alone in seclusion, a reflection arose in his mind thus, "Is it possible to exercise rulership righteously without killing and without instigating others to kill, without confiscating and without instigating others to confiscate, without sorrowing and without causing sorrow?" Then Mara, the evil one, having known with his own mind the reflection in the Blessed One's mind, approached the Blessed One and said to him, "Venerable, sir, let the Blessed One exercise rulership righteously without killing and without instigating others to kill, without confiscating and without instigating others to confiscate, without sorrowing and without instigating others to cause sorrow." And the Buddha said, "For what do you see, evil one, that you speak thus to me?" And he said, "Venerable, sir, the Blessed One has developed and cultivated the four bases of spiritual power or psychic power, made them a vehicle, made them a basis, stabilized them, exercised himself in them, and fully perfected them. And venerable, sir, if the Blessed One wishes, he need only resolve that the Himalayas, the king of mountains, should become gold, and it would turn to gold." And the And the Buddha said, "If there were a mountain made of gold, made entirely of solid gold, not double this would suffice for one. Having known this, bear evenly. How could a person inclined to sensual pleasures, who has seen the source whence suffering springs, having known acquisition or attachment as a tie in the world, a person should train for its removal?" Then Mara, the evil one, realizing "The Blessed One knows me, the fortunate one knows me," sad and disappointed, disappeared right there. So, here, the Buddha one day uh was thinking uh "Is it possible for a king uh to rule according to Dhamma without hurting others?" And then Mara came to tempt him, ask him, "Why don't you become a king?" Then, uh, he also said, "Uh, uh, you you have developed psychic power. Like if you want, uh, the whole Himalayan mountains, uh, can turn into solid gold." And the Buddha said, "Uh, even two Himalayan two Himalayan mountains made of solid gold, uh, is not sufficient, uh, if you are not contented. You have desire and greed." So, that's why the Buddha said, "A person should remove, uh, attachment, remove sensual desire." Actually, uh, in the Bible, Jesus also was tempted by the Mara. Cuz, uh, Jesus was meditating in the desert 40 days and 40 nights. He did not take, uh, food. So, he was meditating and so, Mara was afraid, uh, that he was near to enlightenment enlightenment and brought him up the hills, uh, brought him up the mountains and asked him like to become a king, uh. So, Jesus also refused the temptation. So, it's a little bit similar to this Sutta.
